working_title: Species-specific rainfall sensitivity predicts short-term reassembly of active frog communities
central_claims: Within matched route × seasonal-window comparisons, wetter runs contain more acoustically active species and richness gain increases with rainfall contrast.
Rainfall-associated richness gain is not simple nested addition; exact consecutive-year comparisons show increased compositional turnover with rainfall contrast.

Species wet-versus-dry responses are strongly heterogeneous after pair-level temperature, date, rain-contrast and year-gap adjustment, and more than half of family-matched heterogeneity remains within families.
Species-specific recent-rain sensitivity estimated only from 2001–2007 predicts adjusted wet-versus-dry recruitment estimated independently from 2008–2015.
The temporal prediction persists after family-stratified permutation, supporting persistent species-specific rain-response differences rather than only broad family structure.

mechanism_authority.behavioral_trait: rain_pulse_sensitivity = negative of the within-route dryness slope for run-level acoustic presence during 2001–2007
mechanism_authority.validation_response: adjusted wet-versus-dry species recruitment log odds during 2008–2015

interpretation: Short rainfall pulses are associated with predictable species-selective reassembly of the acoustically active frog community because species differ persistently in their behavioral sensitivity to recent rain.
secondary_results: Pooled body-size association is strong but does not survive family-stratified permutation and is not the mechanism authority.
Coarse hydroperiod flags were nonestimable because all matched species carried both temporary and permanent water flags in the collapsed source.
Earlier participation/residual-association decomposition supports membership-level change more than pairwise co-calling change.
prohibited: rain-pulse sensitivity is a physiological trait
rainfall response strategy is genetically fixed
hydroperiod or breeding-season breadth explains the species response
all species follow the predictive relationship without exceptions
training and validation species are independent species samples
FrogID replicates the matched NAAMP reassembly result
